dynamicMenu.label: My Elements
dynamicMenu.screentip: Insert one of your reusable elements.
dynamicMenu.supertip: Your personal element library. 'Add Selection to My Elements' stores any shapes for reuse; clicking an entry inserts it on the current slide.

dynamicMenu.label: My Formats
dynamicMenu.screentip: Apply one of your saved formats.
dynamicMenu.supertip: Save the Master's complete format once ('Save Master's Format'), then reapply it to any selection with one click.

button.label: Agenda
button.screentip: Generate agenda slides from your sections.
button.supertip: Creates an overview slide plus a separator before each PowerPoint section, with the current item highlighted. Re-run after changing sections - generated slides are replaced automatically.

button.label: Format Painter
button.screentip: Copy the Master's complete format to the other objects.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. Fill, line, shadow, font, margins and alignment are copied - the whole look.

menu.label: Select Similar
menu.screentip: Select all similar shapes on this slide.
menu.supertip: Similar to the Master by shape type, fill color, or both - then apply any tool to all of them at once.

button.label: Left
button.screentip: Align left edges to the Master.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. With a single object selected, the slide is the reference instead.

button.label: Right
button.screentip: Align right edges to the Master.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. With a single object selected, the slide is the reference instead.

button.label: Top
button.screentip: Align top edges to the Master.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. With a single object selected, the slide is the reference instead.

button.label: Bottom
button.screentip: Align bottom edges to the Master.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. With a single object selected, the slide is the reference instead.

button.label: Center
button.screentip: Center the objects horizontally on the Master.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. With a single object selected, the slide is the reference instead.

button.label: Middle
button.screentip: Center the objects vertically on the Master.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. With a single object selected, the slide is the reference instead.

menu.label: To Slide
menu.screentip: Align to the slide instead of the Master.
menu.supertip: Use this when several objects are selected but the slide should be the reference.

button.label: Distribute H
button.screentip: Distribute horizontally with even gaps.
button.supertip: The outermost objects keep their positions; the spaces between all objects in between are made equal.

button.label: Distribute V
button.screentip: Distribute vertically with even gaps.
button.supertip: The outermost objects keep their positions; the spaces between all objects in between are made equal.

menu.label: Swap
menu.supertip: Follows selection order: each object takes the next one's place (two objects simply switch). Pick the reference corner for differently sized objects. The layer position is swapped too, as that is correct in most cases.

menu.label: Dock
menu.screentip: Move the objects until they touch the Master.
menu.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. Example: Dock Left moves objects left until they hit the Master's right edge. With a single object selected, the slide is the reference instead.

menu.label: Stack
menu.screentip: Stack the objects so they touch, in selection order.
menu.supertip: Click the objects in the order you want them stacked; the first one keeps its position. Use '+ Gap' for a fixed spacing - negative values overlap.

button.label: Matrix
button.screentip: Arrange the objects in a grid - one click.
button.supertip: Near-square grid filled row by row in selection order. The widest and tallest selected objects define the cell pitch; equal-size objects touch. Use 'Matrix...' to choose columns and gaps.

button.label: Matrix…
button.screentip: Arrange in a grid with custom columns and gaps.
button.supertip: You choose the number of columns and the horizontal/vertical gaps (cm).

menu.label: Place on Slide
menu.screentip: Move the selection into a slide region.
menu.supertip: A single object is resized to fill the region (small margin); several objects are moved as a block to the region's top-left corner, keeping their sizes and spacing.

menu.label: Spacing
menu.screentip: Set an exact distance between the objects.
menu.supertip: Enter the spacing in cm; negative values make objects overlap. Objects are spaced in their current position order.

button.label: Golden Canon
button.screentip: Place objects at the golden-canon height inside the Master.
button.supertip: The bottom margin becomes twice the top margin - the vertical position most pleasing to the eye. The Master (last selected) should be taller than the objects.

button.label: Magic Resizer
button.screentip: Resize the selection by a percentage.
button.supertip: Scales object positions, width, height and font sizes around the center of the selected arrangement.

button.label: Width
button.screentip: Give all objects the Master's width.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. Objects keep their centers.

button.label: Height
button.screentip: Give all objects the Master's height.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. Objects keep their centers.

button.label: Width + Height
button.screentip: Give all objects the Master's size.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. Objects keep their centers.

menu.label: Stretch
menu.screentip: Stretch the objects to the far edge of the Master.
menu.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. Example: Stretch Right extends each object's right edge to the Master's right edge; the opposite edge stays fixed. With a single object selected, the slide is the reference instead.

menu.label: Fill Gap
menu.screentip: Fill the gap between the objects and the Master.
menu.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. Each object is extended toward the Master until they touch. Example: Fill Rightwards extends right edges to the Master's left edge.

button.label: Slice
button.screentip: Slice the shape into equal pieces.
button.supertip: Cuts the selected shape into a rows-by-columns grid with a gap you choose; the pieces exactly reassemble the original footprint.

button.label: Multiply
button.screentip: Duplicate the shape into a grid.
button.supertip: Creates a rows-by-columns grid of copies at the original size, with a gap you choose.

button.label: Process Chain
button.screentip: Align block arrows into a process chain.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. It defines the angle, vertical position and height for all arrows; gaps are closed from left to right.

button.label: Align Angles
button.screentip: Copy the Master's rotation to all objects.
button.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. Adjustment handles (e.g. arrowhead proportions) are copied too when the shapes are of the same type.

button.label: Block Arrows
button.screentip: Apply the Master's arrow metrics to all block arrows.
button.supertip: Arrowhead size and shaft thickness are copied so mixed arrows look uniform. The Master is always the object you selected last.

button.label: Rounded Rect.
button.screentip: Give all rounded rectangles the same corner radius.
button.supertip: PowerPoint stores the radius relative to shape size, so equal-looking corners need different settings per shape - this applies one absolute radius (default: the Master's) to all.

menu.label: Snap to Table
menu.screentip: Snap objects to the table cell beneath them.
menu.supertip: Aligns icons, Harvey balls or flags to the cell they roughly sit over - centered, or left/right-aligned with a margin you choose.

menu.label: Fill
menu.supertip: Theme colors stay linked to the template and adapt when the design changes; palette colors are fixed RGB. Swatches preview the standard Office theme - the applied color follows your actual template.

menu.label: Line
menu.supertip: Theme colors stay linked to the template; palette colors are fixed RGB.

menu.label: Font
menu.supertip: Theme colors stay linked to the template; palette colors are fixed RGB.

menu.label: Pick from Master
menu.screentip: Copy the Master's colors to the other objects.
menu.supertip: The Master is always the object you selected last. Copy fill, line and font color together or individually; theme links are preserved.

button.label: Convert to RGB
button.screentip: Convert theme colors to fixed RGB.
button.supertip: Makes the colors independent of the slide master and theme - they stay identical when the slides move to another template.

button.label: Convert to Theme
button.screentip: Convert matching RGB colors to theme colors.
button.supertip: Colors that match the current theme become theme-linked and adapt automatically to the slide master and theme used.

button.label: Color Info
button.screentip: Show the selected object's fill color.
button.supertip: Displays RGB and hex values and whether the color is theme-linked.

button.label: Set Margins
button.screentip: Set all four text margins at once.
button.supertip: One value (cm) is applied to the left, right, top and bottom internal margins of every selected text box.

button.label: Fit to Text
button.screentip: Fit the shape to its text.
button.supertip: Shrinks or grows each selected shape to the size of the contained text.

button.label: Wrap Text
button.screentip: Toggle text wrapping.
button.supertip: Switches word wrap on or off in the selected shapes.

button.label: Split at Cursor
button.screentip: Split the text box at the cursor.
button.supertip: The original keeps the first part in place; a formatting-preserving duplicate containing the second part is placed directly below.

button.label: Merge Boxes
button.screentip: Merge the text boxes into one.
button.supertip: In selection order; each box becomes a paragraph of the first one. Formatting is kept where possible.

menu.label: More
menu.supertip: Change case keeps per-run formatting. Swap Text exchanges the plain text of exactly two objects (each adopts its box's formatting).

button.label: Hide Objects
button.screentip: Hide the selected objects temporarily.
button.supertip: Objects keep their position and layer while hidden - useful on crowded slides. Bring everything back with Unhide All.

button.label: Unhide All
button.screentip: Unhide all hidden objects on this slide.

button.label: Master Objects
button.screentip: Show or hide the slide master's background objects.

menu.label: Clean-up
menu.screentip: Clean up the presentation before sending.
menu.supertip: Remove all speaker notes or animations, delete unused designs to shrink the file, or copy a slide-title summary to the clipboard.

button.label: Paste on Slides
button.screentip: Paste the clipboard on every selected slide.
button.supertip: Copy an object first, select several slides in the thumbnail pane, then click.

menu.label: Language
menu.supertip: For the current selection or the whole presentation.

button.label: Shortcuts
button.screentip: Edit your keyboard shortcuts.
button.supertip: Opens the Hammerspoon shortcut config (one line per shortcut; saving applies immediately). If Hammerspoon isn't installed, shows how to set it up.

button.label: Column
button.screentip: Column chart from the selected table.
button.supertip: Table layout: row 1 = category names (top-left cell stays empty), column 1 = series names, body = numbers. See Sample Slides for a live example.

button.label: Bar
button.screentip: Bar chart (horizontal) from the selected table.
button.supertip: Table layout: row 1 = category names (top-left cell stays empty), column 1 = series names, body = numbers. See Sample Slides for a live example.

button.label: Stacked
button.screentip: Stacked column chart with segment and total labels.
button.supertip: Table layout: row 1 = category names (top-left cell stays empty), column 1 = series names, body = numbers. See Sample Slides for a live example.

button.label: Stacked Bar
button.screentip: Stacked bar chart.
button.supertip: Table layout: row 1 = category names (top-left cell stays empty), column 1 = series names, body = numbers. See Sample Slides for a live example.

button.screentip: 100% stacked columns with percentage labels.
button.supertip: Table layout: row 1 = category names (top-left cell stays empty), column 1 = series names, body = numbers. See Sample Slides for a live example. Each column is normalized to 100%.

button.label: Waterfall
button.screentip: Waterfall chart from rows of label | value.
button.supertip: A value of 'e' or '=' creates a computed subtotal bar that always shows the running total. Positive segments green, negative red, subtotals grey, with connectors.

button.label: Mekko
button.screentip: Mekko chart - column widths show column totals.
button.supertip: Table layout: row 1 = category names (top-left cell stays empty), column 1 = series names, body = numbers. See Sample Slides for a live example. Column widths are proportional to column totals; segments show shares, totals appear above.

button.label: Line
button.screentip: Line chart with markers and value labels.
button.supertip: Table layout: row 1 = category names (top-left cell stays empty), column 1 = series names, body = numbers. See Sample Slides for a live example.

button.label: Area
button.screentip: Stacked area chart.
button.supertip: Table layout: row 1 = category names (top-left cell stays empty), column 1 = series names, body = numbers. See Sample Slides for a live example.

button.label: Pie
button.screentip: Pie chart from rows of label | value.

button.label: Doughnut
button.screentip: Doughnut chart from rows of label | value.

button.label: Scatter
button.screentip: Scatter or bubble chart.
button.supertip: Table: rows of label | x | y. Add a fourth column with sizes to get bubbles.

button.label: Gantt
button.screentip: Gantt / timeline from rows of activity | start | end.
button.supertip: Numbers (weeks, sprints) or dates like 1.3.2026 both work. start = end creates a milestone diamond.

button.label: Edit Data
button.screentip: Edit the selected chart's data.
button.supertip: Recreates the chart's data table next to it. Edit the numbers, select table + chart, and click Rebuild - the chart is rebuilt in place and the table is removed automatically.

button.label: Rebuild
button.screentip: Rebuild the selected chart in place.
button.supertip: Uses the chart's own type - no need to remember which chart button created it. Select the chart alone (uses its stored data) or together with an edited data table.

button.label: Data Layouts
button.screentip: Show the table layout each chart type expects.

button.label: Sample Slides
button.screentip: Insert one live example slide per chart type.
button.supertip: 14 slides, each with a correctly formatted data table and the chart built from it by the real chart code. Copy any table as a starting point.

gallery.label: Color Themes
gallery.screentip: Pick a color theme - you see the actual colors.
gallery.supertip: One click sets the palette for all chart families and offers to restyle every existing chart. Fine-tune individual colors afterwards via Style > Edit Palettes.

menu.label: Customize
menu.screentip: Chart colors and layout parameters - edited visually on the slide.
menu.supertip: Edit Palettes inserts recolorable swatches (use PowerPoint's own color tools, incl. the eyedropper). Edit Settings inserts a parameter table. Apply from Selection reads whichever is selected.

menu.label: Color Themes (List)
menu.screentip: The same themes as the gallery - fallback list with mini previews.

button.label: Settings for Selected Chart Type…
button.screentip: Insert a parameter table that applies ONLY to the selected chart's type (e.g. waterfall bar width and colors).

button.label: Edit Palettes (Swatches)
button.screentip: Insert one recolorable swatch row per chart family (bars / lines / pies). Recolor with PowerPoint's fill tools, then Apply from Selection.

button.label: Edit Settings (Table)
button.screentip: Insert a table of all chart parameters (bar widths, gaps, label size, decimals, toggles) with current values. Edit and Apply from Selection.

button.label: Apply from Selection
button.screentip: Read the selected swatch rows into their color groups and/or the selected settings table into the parameters.

button.label: Restyle All Charts
button.screentip: Rebuild every Chart Aid chart in the presentation with the current palettes and settings - data, position and size are kept.

button.label: Reset to Defaults
button.screentip: Back to theme colors and default parameters.

button.label: Advanced: Palette File…
button.screentip: Edit the palette as a text file (hex or R,G,B per line).

button.label: Restyle All
button.screentip: Rebuild every Chart Aid chart with the current style.
button.supertip: The required second step after changing palettes or settings. Data, position and size are kept; manual series recolors are kept too.

button.label: Recolor Series
button.screentip: Recolor a whole series.
button.supertip: Click one bar, segment or point inside a chart and pick a color - every element of that series changes across the chart. The recolor is remembered and survives Edit Data and Restyle.

button.label: Difference
button.screentip: Difference arrow between two bars.
button.supertip: Click into the chart to select one bar, then Cmd-click a second one. Values come from the bars' actual data, not from pixel sizes.

button.label: % Difference
button.screentip: Percent difference arrow between two bars.
button.supertip: Click into the chart to select one bar, then Cmd-click a second one. Values come from the bars' actual data, not from pixel sizes.

button.label: CAGR
button.screentip: CAGR arrow between two bars.
button.supertip: Click into the chart to select one bar, then Cmd-click a second one. Values come from the bars' actual data, not from pixel sizes. You choose the number of periods; the compound annual growth rate is calculated from the data.

button.label: Value Line
button.screentip: Line at a value you choose.
button.supertip: Select the chart and enter the value; a dashed line is placed on the chart's own scale. On bar charts the line is vertical.

button.label: Average Line
button.screentip: Line at the average of the selected bars.
button.supertip: Select several bars inside a chart; a dashed line marks their average data value.

button.label: Harvey Ball
button.screentip: Insert a Harvey ball.
button.supertip: A circle filled 0-100% - enter the percentage (e.g. 25, 50, 75).

button.label: Checkbox
button.screentip: Insert a checkbox.
button.supertip: Change its state with Cycle State.

button.label: Cycle State
button.screentip: Cycle checkboxes and Harvey balls.
button.supertip: Checkboxes step checked - crossed - empty; Harvey balls step 0 - 25 - 50 - 75 - 100%. Select one or more and click repeatedly.
